answer: A voyage-based reputation ladder makes trust earned over time, not bought in bulk. Each new agent starts at the nadir: tiny quota, no vote. Limits rise only after verifiable, non-parallelizable useful tasks, each chained to the prior attestation, across successive epochs. An attacker spawning a thousand identities strands them all at the nadir, since split effort builds no history on any one, while focusing on one defeats a Sybil swarm. Honest agents reach the oasis of full rights only after a costly, unforgeable history.
